title: Playing with Leon Rappolo in Norman Brownlee's band
summary: Wiggs played with Rappolo in Brownlee's band after Rappolo left the New Orleans Rhythm Kings; they discuss where to buy the records.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I'd just like to ask Mr. Johnny Wiggs if he has ever played with the musician Leon Rapolo. Yes, I played with him in Norman Brownlee's band when he came down from Chicago after having finished with the New Orleans Rhythm Kings. Harry Shields was the regular clarinet player, but when he came down, Norman Brownlee hired him for these few jobs that I played with him, with Brownlee. Great, great, of course. And need I say that, I mean, his records, it's obvious from his records.
For those people who've heard them, of course, these things are available. Yeah. They are reissued, and it's a shame that more people haven't heard people like, say, Leon Rapolo. Yeah.
Well, how could I get one of these records?
Can you tell him, Dick? Well, I'll be glad to play them for you on the reissues at Tulane, or you can go down to the Shoppers World Records.

Joe Shallon at 103 Royal. S-H-A-L-O-N. You can try him, because those records are rare, and they're hard to get. But even the reissues become collector's items in a very short time. Okay, thank you very much.
